finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a filename that includes shell metacharacters or commands.
finding.assumptions: The program does not sanitize or validate the filename input before using it to open a file.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is an ifstream constructor (line 18) which opens a file directly using the OS file API, not via a shell or system call. No command execution occurs, so shell metacharacters in the filename cannot influence command execution. The code does not invoke any function that interprets the filename as a command string.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a candidate or party name that includes shell metacharacters or commands.
finding.assumptions: The program does not sanitize or validate the candidate or party names before using them.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported sink is the assignment to an unordered_map entry: parties[candidate] = party; This operation merely stores a string value in a map; it does not invoke any system call, shell command, or function that interprets the string as a command. Since there is no subsequent use of the stored strings in a command execution context within the provided fragment, there is no path from the untrusted input to a command execution sink. Therefore, OS Command Injection cannot occur here.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a vote that includes shell metacharacters or commands.
finding.assumptions: The program does not sanitize or validate the vote input before using it.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the sink at line 41: votes[vote]++; this operation only increments a counter in an unordered_map keyed by the string 'vote'. No system call, exec, or shell invocation is performed. Therefore, the string content cannot influence OS command execution. No other code paths invoke a command interpreter. The claim of OS command injection is unfounded.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can control the winner variable, which could include shell metacharacters or commands.
finding.assumptions: The program does not sanitize or validate the winner variable before using it in the output.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The sink is a simple stream output to std::cout, which merely writes the string to the console. No system call, exec, or similar function that would interpret the string as a command is invoked. Therefore, even if the "winner" variable contains shell metacharacters or arbitrary text, it cannot lead to command execution. The code does not pass the string to any OS command interface, so the reported OS Command Injection claim is unfounded.
